entry_points.text: Probe initialization rejects type mismatch, requires privilege, refuses branch sampling, decodes return and offset fields for the lower constructor and installs teardown; breakpoint delivery forwards a single count with the breakpoint address when hardware is running and exclusion accepts.

Open validates flags, attributes, security, kernel-sampling, namespace, frequency, physical-address and lockdown rules, resolves control-group, processor and lively task targets with inheritance consistency, then installs under guards; tracepoint permission combines paranoid level, privilege and the security hook.

Migration detaches pinned then flexible members between processors with quiescence and reinstalls siblings before leaders; task exit clears ownership with release ordering, tears down task context with exit reporting, forwards records to processor-wide contexts and detaches system-wide data.

exports.text: Tracepoint delivery refreshes the shared buffer for the record type, walks subscribers under read-copy-update and forwards accepted ones through the software path with a reinitialized sample, and when a foreign task is given also walks its pinned and flexible groups before releasing the recursion handle.
Tracepoint unit registration has an active build that publishes tracepoint, kernel-probe and user-probe units with fixed or dynamic types behind feature guards, and an empty build that does nothing.

Blocking program attachment serializes the underlying setter with the context lock, with an alternate build reporting unsupported; release is a no-op without a program and otherwise separates non-tracing release from tracing detach, with an alternate no-op build.

Unit registration validates name and scope, assigns a numeric type, optionally creates a device, allocates per-processor contexts with locality, installs default operations and publishes for lookup; removal unpublishes, drains grace periods, refuses busy when live events remain with an unmapped callback, otherwise detaches all events and frees storage.
Module reference acquisition succeeds immediately without an owner, otherwise requires a live module and a successful reference increment from non-zero, tracing success.

Kernel-internal creation bypasses descriptors and grouping, guards unit lifetime and installs immediately after tombstone, online and exclusivity checks; file helpers validate the operations table before returning the file, event or embedded attributes.

hazards.text: Blocking timer cancel from inside its own callback would deadlock, avoided with a non-blocking attempt plus a stopped flag; reusing one sample across deliveries would carry suppressing flags, avoided by reinitializing before each forward.

Filter application may meet tombstone or memory-less tasks and then returns early or restarts without touching ranges; creation aborts without live mutation on cross-unit or cross-processor reuse, nesting, clock mismatch, tombstoned or offline targets.

Detachment clears ownership to convert later use into a fault and orders mapping creation against revocation; removal reports busy rather than forcing live events with an unmapped callback; group relocation releases old references then reinstalls siblings before the leader so leader-driven enabling never observes stale context.
Registration warns once and rejects invalid name or scope, warns on fixed-type mismatch and propagates device, allocation and publication failures.

invariants.text: Tracepoint delivery requires preemption disabled and breakpoint delivery requires interrupts disabled; the software timer skips excluded events including configured idle-task exclusion.

Foreign-task filtering requires configuration to match the record type and rejects synchronous-trap requests; filter teardown assumes quiescence; file-backed application scans mapped areas to completion; scope resolves core, die, cluster, package and system masks or yields nothing.

A unit becomes visible only after full preparation; removal unpublishes before detaching so only complete events are torn down; identifier exchange validates the old value; teardown removes files and devices then scans possible processors; reclamation drains the membership list and waits for emptiness.

Event initialization acquires a module reference, orders group-leader locking, invokes unit-specific setup, enforces extended-register capability, exclusion prohibition and topology intersection; type normalization prefers the parent, decodes generic encodings with raw fallback and scans the unit list on missing aliases.

Allocation validates processor and trap-task rules, prepares synchronization and references, enforces auxiliary, control-group, filter, callchain, security and accounting steps; global counters track requested features with special tickless and scheduling-branch handling; clocks map five identifiers with non-maskable safety rules; permission combines monitoring capability with ptrace and kill checks.

Creation refuses sampling on non-interrupt units, requires leaders to be self-led with matching clock, processor, context and liveness and no exclusive or pinned newcomer flags, allows software into hardware groups while relocating pure-software groups toward hardware and refusing cross-unit hardware mixing, orders output, size, auxiliary and exclusivity checks before file creation, and marks kernel handles with a tombstone while refusing auxiliary requests.

Task teardown deschedules when exiting, clears linkage, marks tombstone, optionally emits exit records and walks members; non-exit reuse waits for a single reference; delayed release asserts no remaining context.

Inheritance links to the original ancestor, skips revoked or exited ancestry, mirrors enable state, copies period and overflow handling for frequency mode, creates leader then members tolerating orphaned leaders, validates auxiliary linkage, and respects clone and signal-trap flags while recording completeness.

This scope relies on external helpers for device data, sysfs formatting, time conversion, per-processor access, local counters, masking, clocks, warnings, register access, barriers, lists, tasks, files and security hooks; their contracts are owned elsewhere and cited here only to preserve the dependency.

locks.text: Identifier and list changes serialize with a dedicated mutex; membership changes use a per-unit spinlock; creation holds nested sleepable and regular read-side sections across lookup while removal synchronizes both domains before reclaim.

Task creation holds the execution-update read guard across permission validation and installation; context mutation, tombstone and online checks and installation serialize with the context mutex; teardown holds it across descheduling and member exit while lookup relies on install-time checks.

Foreign-task delivery holds a read-side section plus the target context spinlock; migration holds both source and destination mutexes with an extra destination reference and quiescence when anything moved; inheritance guards orphan checks and linkage; sideband appends use a per-list spinlock with read-copy-update insertion.

Range application skips tombstones, references memory only for file filters, rebuilds ranges under an interrupt-safe lock, bumps generation and restarts; multiplex updates validate a minimum, then rewrite unit and per-processor intervals under a dedicated mutex and processor-set read lock; frequency accounting uses atomics with tickless and scheduling-branch slow paths.

state_machines.text: The software timer stops for inactive or halted events, otherwise samples with last period and interrupt registers subject to exclusion, advances by the clamped period with a 10000-nanosecond minimum and continues unless overflow terminates; start consumes saved remainder or clamped period, cancel preserves remainder with a non-blocking attempt, destroy cancels unconditionally, and initialization sets a monotonic relative timer while folding frequency mode into a fixed period.

Processor-clock and task-clock events accumulate elapsed time, seed stamps and arm timers on start, disarm with optional update on stop, support add with optional start, delete as updating stop and read as update, and accept only their own type and clock configuration while rejecting branch sampling; task reads compose context stamp plus elapsed performance time.

Default transaction handlers are empty with zero or success results; generic start records flags and disables only for add-only transactions with symmetric commit and cancel re-enable and a zero default index; device allocation binds to the event-source bus with release unwinding; detachment revokes, orders mapping creation, frees tracing and filter resources, invokes destroy once, drops references and clears ownership before list removal.

Migrated members at least in off state normalize to inactive before reinstall with siblings before leaders and updated assignment; task teardown deschedules, tombstones, emits exit records and walks members for exit handling.

structs.text: Kernel-probe and user-probe units use software task context with trace add and delete plus software lifecycle routing; the former exposes a return-flag format attribute and the latter adds a reference-offset attribute; configuration reserves the low bit for return marking and the top 32 bits for the offset.

Unit devices expose type, multiplex interval, filter count and processor mask with visibility rules hiding empty filter counts and unscoped masks; processor-clock and task-clock units share software context, advertise no non-maskable support and route lifecycle to clock handlers.

Unit state carries identity, scope, owner, device, per-processor table, transaction and enable operations, membership list, exclusivity, capabilities, filter count, topology accessor and unmapped callback; event state carries placement, attributes, grouping, ownership, lifecycle, task, clock, overflow handling, sampling, filters, synchronization and list nodes.

Address-filter text parsing uses three actions plus a none value, four sources and three parser states, with a vocabulary mapping filter, start and stop words and numeric patterns with optional file suffixes.

Creation defines a flag mask with close-on-exec, control-group, output and no-group modifiers, negative sentinels for unspecified task or processor, a control-group selector flag, five clock choices with distinct safety, and conventional permission, argument, device, busy, sampling, size and descriptor failures.
